title: low-precision-path-allocator-and-kernel-hookups
author: Luca Ortega
description:
Motivation: Continued work to reduce per-token cost and tail latency for low-precision inference. Prior PRs added isolated INT8/FP8 kernels and dequant fusion primitives; this change weaves those pieces into the serving runtime with a small, deterministic allocator and dispatch layer that routes requests to the best low-precision execution path based on model variant, sequence-length distribution, KV-cache state, and batching profile. The goal is pragmatic: improve throughput and p99 latency for production workloads while preserving correctness and fast fallback to FP16/FP32 when numerical risk is detected.

Summary of changes (single-shot): adds a LowPrecisionPathAllocator that makes per-request routing decisions, wires kernel dispatch tables for INT8 and FP8 fused-dequant paths, introduces lightweight per-worker hints to the continuous-batching scheduler to avoid head-of-line blocking when long sequences and small batches mix, and optimizes KV cache hot-path bookkeeping to reduce CPU overhead on cache-miss heavy workloads. Also includes microbench harness changes and canary rollout config for safe production enablement.

Why this is different: previous PRs provided kernels and fusion infra in isolation; this PR focuses on connecting those kernels into runtime scheduling and KV-cache-aware routing so that benefits are realized in end-to-end serving. It emphasizes deterministic allocation (no global locks), low-overhead decision logic, and explicit fallback rules when stability checks fail.

Behavioral details and invariants: allocator decisions are per-request at enqueue time and are stable for the request lifetime; dequant fusion is only selected when the model variant metadata marks weights as stable for fusion and dynamic range checks pass for the first token; KV cache uses an additional small per-request bitmap to avoid expensive lookups for fully warmed prefixes. Fallback to FP16 is immediate and logged when a numerical anomaly (NaN/Inf or outlier token likelihood shift exceeding a threshold) is detected.

Benchmark highlights (internal perf harness, 8xA100 p4d-like profile, mixed sequence lengths): INT8 fused-dequant path: +12% throughput, p99 latency -18% on chat-like traffic compared to baseline FP16 runtime; FP8 path: +8% throughput, p99 -10% for short-sequence-only workloads; KV cache bookkeeping optimization reduces CPU-side cache-miss accounting overhead by ~25% in high-concurrency tests. End-to-end cost projection (model-dependent) shows unit token cost reduction up to 20% in aggressive INT8 mode under production batching distributions. Full benchmark run artifacts attached to the PR.

Compatibility and safety: feature gated behind runtime flag low_precision.path_enabled and staged via canary config (release/ops/rollouts). No model format changes required. Contains extensive checks that prevent low-precision selection for models listed in a denylist or when model metadata lacks quant-stability hints.

Testing: unit tests for allocator heuristics, kernel routing, and fallback; integration tests with the continuous-batching scheduler and KV cache; regression tests exercising numerical stability thresholds. CI includes microbench regression checks on the perf lab.

How to exercise locally: run tools/perf/harness --profile=canary-int8 --model=gpt-medium --seq-distribution=chat-mix; the harness supports toggling low_precision.path_enabled. See docs/perf/low_precision_readme.md for experiment configuration and metrics artifacts.

References: related Linear ticket ENG-2145, earlier kernel PRs that added fused-dequant primitives and FP8 kernels.

Release strategy: deploy to a 5% canary for 48h with end-to-end latency/cost monitors and automatic rollback if p99 regresses beyond the configured SLO delta.

Checklist:
- [x] runtime allocator and dispatch implemented
- [x] kernel hookups and fused-dequant path enabled behind flag
- [x] KV cache bookkeeping optimization implemented
- [x] unit and integration tests added
- [x] perf harness runs and artifacts committed

Notes: this PR intentionally avoids aggressive auto-quant decisions; quant selection remains model-owner controlled until we have more confidence from cross-customer benchmarks.

review_comments: Priya Menon: Can you add a short experiment that shows when the allocator would prefer FP16 despite INT8 availability? Reason: we need a clear example to justify operator overrides.
Luca Ortega: Added a test case that simulates a model with unstable dynamic ranges and verified the allocator chooses FP16; expanded the readme with an operator override note.
Sara Kim: The continuous-batching hint looks good; are there pathological cases where this increases tail latency? Suggest a stress test with interleaved very long sequences.

Luca Ortega: Added a stress bench in tools/perf and updated scheduler comments. Stress tests show minimal regression when long sequences are rare; if long sequences dominate, we fallback to a conservative scheduling mode.
Daniel Park: KV cache bitmap is elegant — can you confirm memory overhead per worker?
Luca Ortega: Bitmap is 64 bytes per request slot by default (configurable); added comment and a unit test asserting memory bounds.
Priya Menon: Approved after perf data added.
release_notes: Introduces a runtime-low-precision allocator that routes requests to INT8/FP8 fused-dequant kernels when safe, reduces p99 latency and improves throughput for many production batching patterns; gated behind feature flag and staged via canary rollout. See docs/perf/low_precision_readme.md for usage.
